record.context_brief: Krylov solvability for one-dimensional Friedrichs operators
record.original_question: Investigate when the inverse problem Af = g is Krylov-solvable for the prototypical Friedrichs operator on H = L^2(R) given by dom A = H^1(R) and Af = -f' + f, and more generally for first-order operators of the form A = -d/dx + c(x) where c : R -> C is chosen so that c(x) + overline{c(x)} is a positive bounded function separated from zero. The problem is to identify suitable assumptions on the datum g and, in the variable-coefficient case, on the coefficient c under which Krylov solvability holds.

evidence.quote: Consider for instance this very prototypical Friedrichs operator: the complex Hilbert space H = L^2(R), and dom A := H^1(R), Af := −f' + f.
More generally, one may consider variants where A acts as A = − d/dx + c(x) for c : R → C such that c(x) + c(x) is a positive bounded function separated from zero.
QUESTION 3: To investigate the Krylov-solvability of the inverse problem Af = g induced by (4.4) or (4.5) (or variants) under suitable conditions on g and c.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H = L^2(\mathbb{R})$ be the complex Hilbert space of square-integrable functions on the real line, and let $A$ be the densely defined linear operator on $H$ with domain $\operatorname{dom} A = H^1(\mathbb{R})$ (the Sobolev space of $L^2$-functions whose distributional derivative is in $L^2$) acting by
$$Af = -f' + f.$$
More generally, for a measurable function $c : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that $c(x) + \overline{c(x)} = 2\operatorname{Re} c(x)$ is bounded and bounded away from zero (i.e., there exist constants $0 < m \le M < \infty$ with $m \le 2\operatorname{Re} c(x) \le M$ for almost every $x$), consider the operator
$$A f = -f' + c(x) f, \qquad \operatorname{dom} A = H^1(\mathbb{R}).$$
For $g \in \operatorname{ran} A$, the Krylov subspace associated to $A$ and $g$ is
$$\mathcal{K}(A,g) = \overline{\operatorname{span}\{g, Ag, A^2 g, \ldots\}}^{\,\|\cdot\|_H},$$
defined whenever $g \in \bigcap_{n\ge 0} \operatorname{dom} A^n$. The inverse problem $Af = g$ is said to be Krylov-solvable if it admits a solution $f \in \operatorname{dom} A$ which belongs to $\mathcal{K}(A,g)$.

Problem: Identify explicit sufficient conditions on the datum $g$ (and, in the variable-coefficient case, on the coefficient $c$) under which the inverse problem $A f = g$ is Krylov-solvable for the above operators.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open question in a 2024 work on open problems and perspectives for solving Friedrichs systems via Krylov approximation. Related general results on Krylov solvability of unbounded operators exist, and recent work (2024–2025) on Friedrichs systems on intervals addresses kernel structure, but no published resolution of Krylov-solvability for this prototypical one-dimensional Friedrichs operator $-d/dx + c(x)$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ has been located.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and perspectives on solving Friedrichs systems by Krylov approximation
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems on Krylov solvability of Friedrichs systems, including the prototypical first-order operator on L^2(R).
status_evidence.claim: The Krylov-solvability of this prototypical Friedrichs operator is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Friedrichs systems on an interval
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results on kernel dimensions for one-dimensional Friedrichs operators in terms of coefficient values at endpoints.
status_evidence.claim: Related recent work addresses one-dimensional Friedrichs operators but does not resolve Krylov-solvability.

status_evidence.title: Krylov Solvability of Unbounded Inverse Linear Problems
status_evidence.snippet: General abstract framework for Krylov solvability of unbounded inverse problems.
status_evidence.claim: General abstract criteria exist but are not specialized to the Friedrichs operator -d/dx + c(x).
